source: You burned Lincoln's envelope.
Bocco liked that.
Bocco claims he didn't see anything.
Bocco claims a group of teenagers did it.
Bocco claims he saw a mechanic working on the clock.
Ah, I saw you repair the clock. Well done, young man. Restoring what is broken and returning things to normal is a virtue, you know.
[Mutter] You don't say.
Aw, shit. Guess I better take it apart again. [Leave]
Oh yeah, I'm all about being a good, virtuous little lad. That's me. Virtue Boy.
Oh wow, I never would've thought. Listen, let's talk about something else real quick...
A swell shot? The Solstice campfires are an important part of our faith, boy. If you're taking a picture, you need to ensure you capture the gravitas of the situation.
...Which is?
(INVESTIGATIVE) Don't worry. I'll ensure to frame the fire as the central piece of the picture, with you tending to it as a devout follower.
Thanks papa
(SOCIAL) I was thinking of trying to capture the street behind you, to show all the people making their way towards the light.
...Hrm.
[Shoot finger pistols at him and leave]
Virtue Boy, out! [Run away]
Say, I got a question for you...
Oh? And which one is that?
The one in West End. You know, the one that looks like a church.
The, uh, blue one.
I don't know yet, but I can't wait to find out. I love learning about the Shepherd. He's so cool.
...And then take copies and sell them, so I can donate the profit to the church, of course.
[Smile as cutely as you can]
Yup, uh, definitely a given.

The place of the Shepherd in this modern age! The shining beacon of truth, order, and justice — one that braves the elements and shines a light on the path of each and all who are pious enough to walk it.
...And it's loyal tender, of course, who places his time and his life in the hands of the loving Shepherd. Or, you know. Something like that.
(INVESTIGATIVE) Don't worry. I'll ensure to frame the fire as the central piece of the picture, with you tending to it as a devout follower.
Yeah, uh...that. That's what I'm going for.
(SOCIAL) I was thinking of trying to capture the street behind you, to show all the people making their way towards the light.
...How sharply observed of you, boy. Perhaps I did judge you too harshly.
[Nod piously]
Most definitely. So is that a go-ahead on the picture, then?
Honestly, man? I think you had me all figured out. Can I still take the picture?
Hrm! Not a bad idea at all. I enjoy the symbolism immensely. All citizens, united, seeking out the guiding light of the Shepherd. Yes, very good.
[Nod piously]
So is that a yes, or...?
Sweet. Now scoot over - there's a particularly sad-looking lady coming up behind you.
That's very beautiful. Very beautiful, indeed.
[Wipe away a tear and nod]
Yes. I am religious boy.
Really? Oh, man. Good. I was just kind of winging that one.
...Is that so? And what exactly is the purpose of that picture, then? What do you plan on doing with it?
Well, my final project is all about, uh, how kids today have forgot about the teachings of the Shepherd. It's to remind them of His presence.
I was thinking of donating it to my local church.
Develop it, I guess. Maybe that's a given.
Alright, you've convinced me. Take your picture.
[Take picture]
Pictures? On this holy night? Hrm. What of, exactly?
Grandfather Steam.
Not sure yet. It's for a project.
People, mostly.

By Shepherd's flame! Young people these days... Yes, the darkest day of the year, in many a way. Hence the fire, hence the masks. Where do you live? Who is your priest? I'd like to have a word with him.
I'm not much of a believer. Sorry.
I live in the dorms, I guess. I'm a student.
Our neighbourhood priest was a mean drunk.
Very well. It'd be wrong of me to deny someone who is trying so clearly to do his duty.
[Take a picture]
All done? I confess, I'm not too familiar with the...art of photography.
(SARCASTIC) Oh, praise be. This will be a picture most holy.
Don't worry. I'm very talented.
[Shrug] We won't know until I've developed it.
...Don't get your hopes up.

That's right: Nightcoming...the Dark Eve, the Winter Solstice. The coldest and darkest day of the year!  A night of victory for the Shepherd and defeat for all the unholy. The flame's triumph over the night.
...Night of victory?
Who are the unholy, exactly?
Triumph over the what now?
Hrm. Hello there, young man. I see you're not wearing a mask. It's Winter Solstice today, don't you know?
Hard to take pictures with a mask on, old man.
I'm aware. That's why I'm out taking pictures.
...Winter Solstice?
Hrm.
Mind if we keep this conversation going? I'm really enjoying myself, if you couldn't tell.
Anyway. Good luck with salvation, man. [Leave]
Pah. Is Father Niall not tending to the herd? Or are you kids skipping out on sermons? It wouldn't be surprise me, not a bit.
I'm skipping sermons right now, in fact.
He's got more of an off-hand approach. We like it that way.
As I said, son: those deviants down the street were loitering around it before I told them to leave. I'd have a stern word with them, if I were you.
Uh-huh. I will. Very stern. Sterningly stern.
What's your problem with those kids again?
Winter Solstice is a very sacred night, boy. I take this duty seriously. I can keep an eye on it now, if you think whoever did it will be back. We can't have vandalism in this neighbourhood.
Sure. Thanks.
Sure. See you later.
Well, I certainly saw those young women standing around it earlier. Smoking, swearing... deviants, all of them! What is the younger generation coming to, I ask?
What indeed. Thanks.
I don't know. You tell me.
Nonsense. A man of the cloth wouldn't drink, it's forbidden! Don't be disrespectful of your elders, boy.
Ask anyone, they'll tell you the same thing.
Not much of a believer? Tsk tsk. Faith isn't a pastime you can pick and choose, you know. It's a virtue.
Guess I'm not very virtuous.
Way I see it, I can't make myself believe. Sorry.
I don't care about any of this, old man.
Like I said, the only one I saw touching the clock was that mechanic down the street. Did you speak to him?
Not yet, but I will.
It just doesn't seem likely that he'd be the culprit. What, he secretly destroys clocks during work hours? Think he gets off on it?

Not anyone who would leave it in a state of disrepair. Quite the opposite, actually. A mechanic came by a short while ago. Left down the way you came. If you hurry down the street, you might still catch him.
Huh. Thanks.
Sure he wasn't an anti-clockist in disguise?
Hush with your nonsense. I know what I saw.
If you say so, old man.
I'm sure. See you later. [Leave]
Hello again, young man. Feeling the cold begin to creep up your bones?
I was hoping to talk to you.
No, I'm peachy. See ya.

They seek acceptance from their peers in all the worst ways. Delinquents and mischief makers. Smoking at that age... I'll wager they haven't been to church in years! Mark my words, I'll pray for them and their families.
Yeah, smoking at that age? What's the world coming to, huh? Not me, though. I'm a good boy.
You do that. I'll go do the same. [Leave]
Hrm. So, you've come to warm yourself by the fire?
I'm not cold.
...It is kind of nice, actually.
Depends. Can I stand here in peace and quiet?
Hrm. Is there some sort of symbolism you're trying to achieve? Pictures of time on the darkest night of the year?
Oh yeah. That.
[Lie] Yes. Definitely.
Nah. It just looks cool in the evening.
Make sure they're wearing their masks. Can't have someone running around ruining the sanctity of the occasion by making people reveal themselves.
It'll be fine.
Yes, sir.
[Shrug]
A project, eh? Hrm. Very well. Hard work should never be looked down upon. You'd better make it worth your while. Wasteful work, however, is a sin against both time and the Shepherd himself.
Oh, wasting time? Me? Never.
It will be worthwhile. Once I finish this, I get to graduate.

You might not be, but I saw your friend over there, shivering. A night like this is no time to trade warmth for fashion — a vanity I see repeated by many of the young people that come to warm themselves here.
Larry? He's fine. Just tired.
Larry isn't vain. Neither am I.
Tell me about it. Those young people, huh? Scoundrels, all of them.
...This is the flame of the Shepherd, my boy. The start and the end of all things. We are made by fire, and we die in flame. This warmth is what sustains us. The love of the Shepherd.
I didn't ask for a lecture. My hands are just cold.
[Say nothing and warm your hands by the fire]
You see, many seek out the comfort of the Shepherd without wanting to devote themselves to Him. They think it's a comfort given to them. But no! It has to be earned.
Guess I'll go earn it, then. Later, old man.
Earned how, exactly?
Hrm. "Those who sit by the fire do well to sing its praises, for the ungrateful are forever ignorant in the eyes of the Shepherd."
...Yeah, I got to go. See ya.
[Nod along and warm your hands]
..Which means?
Hrm.
You know, actually, since I've got your attention...
[Leave]
I'm sure he can decide that for himself.
Probably. Look, I'm gonna go.
Forget about Larry. Can I ask you about some stuff?
I'll ask him. How about that?
And yet here you are, dressed like it's September. You look like you need some warm comfort, both of you.
I'm fine. So is Larry.
[Ignore him and warm yourself by the fire]
I mean, if it's free. I don't need to donate anything, do I?
Like I said: by devotion. By living a virtuous life, following the tenets of the scripture, and by singing His praises.
That's going to be a pass from me.
I'll be honest with you, gramps, I don't really know the scripture.
Aw, shucks. My doctor says I'm not supposed to have tenets.
Not much of a singer.
Don't get cute with me, boy. Prayer, of course, is a fine start, but the true core of devotion lies in keeping the Shepherd and his teachings in your mind and heart at all times.
No offence, man, but I don't think the Shepherd would be too pleased with what's on my mind.
So what, go to church? Confess your sins? Be a good citizen.
Then I'll go do just that. Later, old man.
Then read it, boy. Ignorance is no excuse for indolence.
(INVESTIGATIVE) And eloquence is no substitute for wisdom.
(SARCASTIC) Yeah? Well, that's just like, your opinion, man.
(SOCIAL) Eh. If I learn something, I'd rather learn it from people.
...Cool. I'll go read, then. Later, old man.
Hrm. Perhaps I judged you a little harshly, son. You may be clever, but intelligence is a virtue only when it is put to good use. Are you putting it to good use?
That depends. I'd like to ask you about some things.
Very rarely.
I was just about to. See you later, old man.
It's the truth, boy. No opinion can sway it.
In that case, mind if we change the subject?
Great. This has been an incredibly productive conversation. [Leave]
Oh? Well then, my door is always open. Is there something I can help you with right now?
Sure. Mind if I ask you some questions?
Nope. Later.
Hrm?
Oh, by the way. My friend's not interested in your fire.
Mind if I take a picture of you?
That's all. Goodbye.
I got this envelope I'm supposed to destroy. Mind if I throw it in the fire?
Any idea what happened to the clock?
So, this whole Shepherd thing...
Yes. Most certainly.
...Pass.
I was being...what's the word? Hyperbolic?
Off to church I go, then. Bye.
So what, if I go to church I'll be saved?
Sacrilegious, more like.
Hah. You got me.
So, all I got to do is attend some sermons? Is that right?
Oh yeah. One of my better qualities.
If your heart is truly in it, then yes.
I'll give it some thought, how about that?
Oh, man. Salvation is easy.
Oh. Bummer. Well, see ya.
Hrm. And may I ask why?
Probably better if you don't.
Oh, you know. He's just done being called a lazy sinner.
He thinks you're peddling shit. So, you know.
Hrm. Deviants, all of you.
So true. Well, I'm off to deviate. Later.
...Oh man, he knew you'd say that.
[Nod solemnly and leave]
It depends on what you're burning.
Just some old...bills.
Oh, you know. Sinful stuff.
Hrm. Go ahead.
Thanks, Shepherd. You're baller.
[Loudly] Goodbye, porn collection.
Thanks. [Throw it in]
...Then I am pleased. Well done, lad. I'm glad to see you've come around to respect your elders, and above all, the Shepherd.
...Uh-huh. Well, I'm off to go sing praises. Later, old man.
Oh yeah. I love that shit.
Of course, father. Papa. Daddy.
You must understand, this isn't just a bonfire. It's a beacon of the Shepherd's light.
So is that a no, or...?
Oh, sorry. Mind if I throw this envelope in the beacon of the Shepherd's light?
[Toss it in, grin, and run away]
Then I shall wait and see. Patience is a virtue, don't you know?
Uh-huh. Say, can we talk about something else?
[Mutter] Of course it fucking is.
Enjoy the wait. See ya.
Faith, son. Trust in your ability, and others will trust in it, too.
...Okay. Let me ask you some thing else.
[Mutter] Yes, daddy.
That's...actually not bad advice. Thanks.
...Hold on.
[Run away]
Oops, slip of the tongue. Mind if we change the subject?
Hrm. Very well. Come by the church, up the road, when you have it developed. I should like to see it.
I should think you do. See ya.
We'll see. Mind if I ask you something else?
[Mutter] Oh yeah, that's very fucking likely.
...What was that?
Nothing. Can I ask you something?
Oh, I was just being a dick to you. That's why I said it so quietly. Anyway, bye!
Me? I didn't say nothing. I was just leaving.
Of course, my son. Anything else I can do for you?
I did want to ask you something...
Nah, I'm good. Later.
Well, as scripture teaches us, the dark Goddess of the night came three times to steal from the Shepherd.
[Say nothing and listen]
...Oh, you don't have to tell the whole story.
Did she succeed?
...A picture? Of me? Of the fire? Dare I ask why?
The lighting is really good. I just think it'd make for a swell shot.
(SARCASTIC) Oh, you know. I'm really keen on our lord and saviour, the Shepherd. Call it an act of worship.
...Nevermind, actually.
First, she came for his staff, hoping to break and disparage all order and justice. The Shepherd fended her off and sent her back into the darkness.
That sent her running, huh?
...And you're telling me the whole story. Great.
Mhm. Then what?
Then, she came for His flame, to rob His followers of His warmth and care. Again, the Shepherd fought her off into the night.
Wow, the Shepherd is so cool.
What a loving and caring act.
What about the third time? There's always a third time.

The third time, she came for both — as well as his light. But when the Shepherd fought her off once more, she realized that light, warmth, and order are all concordantly opposed to the night. There was no way for her to beat him.
Let's go, Shepherd. Kick her ass.
That's not much of a story.
[Shrug]

Instead, she now comes for his followers. During the darkest night of the year, when her malice and jealousy culminates, the dark Goddess creeps into the shadows to spread lies and doubt, hoping to turn us against the Shepherd.
And you believe all this?
And the Shepherd just...lets that happen?
...It's over? Thank Shepherd. I'm out. [Leave]
Well, when the night Goddess comes crawling through the shadows, she spreads rumours and lies about each and all of us. She listens, and knows us all by name and face.
She knows my face and name?
Oh, right. I remember this story now. Let's, uh, change the subject.
How?
...And the masks?
Do you not know the story of the three nights of Winter Solstice, my boy?
This thing...tonight, you mean?
I do not, but I assume you're going to tell me.
[Lie] Uh...sure.
Of course I do. It's right, and righteous. Even if it were only a parable, you would do well to listen to it. Learn something.
I'll ask a better question, how's that?
What's the moral of a story where your god allows you to get spied on and lied to?
...Yes?
..."Winter Solstice"?
What's up with all the masks, again?
...Actually, that's enough about the Shepherd for now.
The Shepherd believes in you and me. What is our faith and our devotion worth, if it never was tested? If virtue was easy, it wouldn't be virtue.
So you don't really have an answer. Neat. Can I ask you something else?
I'm just saying, it doesn't seem like a kind and loving god would let his worshipers deal with that kind of shit.
...Okay, we're done here. [Leave]
Spare the rod, spoil the child.
Fantastic. Let me ask you something else, instead.
Well, I've had plenty of rod, and I'm still fucked up.
You're nuts. [Leave]
Hrm. Language.
Fine. Let's talk about something else.
Fuck off. [Leave]
Well, when the night Goddess comes crawling through the shadows, she spreads rumours and lies about each and all of us. She listens, and knows us all by name and face.
She knows my face and name?
How?
...And the masks?

Every time a poor sinner complains, you see, she's there to listen and worsen his hurt. She knows what ails us because we are so vocal about it. That's why it's a virtue to carry your burdens with grace and silence.
Bottle it all up. Solid advice, father.
So we stay quiet so she doesn't know our names — and the masks are for our faces?
Let me ask you something else.
We wear them to trick and confuse the Goddess. This way, she doesn't know who's who, and her lies fall flat.
Right, right. I have another question for you.
So how come you aren't wearing a mask?
Right. Thanks for the reminder, man. [Leave]
There is honour in remaining stoic and unmoved in the face of great tragedies or sorrow.
As well as expensive therapy bills. Later, man. [Leave]
And the masks are for what, again?
Oh, yeah. Wearing masks makes me so, so stoic.
...I've got another question for you.
I'm a man of the Shepherd, through and through. By being here, tending to His fire, I'm already more than safe from the corruption of the Goddess. And from temptation.
Sure, but aren't the masks kind of fun?
So you think. [Wink]
Good for you. [Leave]
Fun doesn't factor into virtue.
Figured. Listen, I had another question about the Shepherd.
I've been busy tending to the fire and the lost souls that gather around it. What of the clock?
It's missing a hand. Did you see anyone fiddling around with it?
Hrm.
...Let's, uh, talk some more about the Shepherd.
[Awkwardly step away]
Hrm. Are you being quite honest with me, boy? Until now, you've seemed to be quite like the kids you talk about.
I'm just very socially anxious. I lash out at authority figures. My bad.
Me? No, that must've been someone else. I love the Shepherd.
Oh yeah, sorry about that. Hah. Don't know what came over me.
What was that?
Nothing. See you later.
Oh, uh, I was asking you a question...
